title_eng: Feature Location Restoration for Under-Sampled Photoplethysmogram Using Spline Interpolation
title_kor: Feature Location Restoration for Under-Sampled Photoplethysmogram Using Spline Interpolation
abstract:
The purpose of this research is to restore the feature location of under-sampled photoplethysmogram using spline
interpolation and to investigate feasibility for feature shape restoration. We obtained 10 kHz-sampled photoplethysmogram and
decimated it to generate under-sampled dataset. Decimated dataset has 5 kHz, 2.5 k Hz, 1 kHz, 500 Hz, 250 Hz, 25 Hz and 10
Hz sampling frequency. To investigate the restoration performance, we interpolated under-sampled signals with 10 kHz, then
compared feature locations with feature locations of 10 kHz sampled photoplethysmogram. Features were upper and lower
peak of photplethysmography waveform. Result showed that time differences were dramatically decreased by interpolation.
Location error was lesser than 1 ms in both feature types. In 10 Hz sampled cases, location error was also deceased a lot,
however, they were still over 10 ms.
